scripts.epicurean:
I'm sure y'all have seen this graph before. And if you haven't, according to this graph, the God of the Bible shouldn't even exist. Sounds crazy, right? But look at the argument.

If God is all powerful, He can stop evil. If He's all knowing, He knows about evil. And if He's all good, He should want to stop it. So why does evil exist?

Well, there's something this graph leaves out. Free will. Think about it. If God controlled every decision you made, would you really have a choice?

You couldn't lie, steal, or hurt anyone, because God would stop you. But then you wouldn't be choosing good either.
scripts.water:
Ever wonder where rain actually comes from? Look at this diagram. The sun heats the ocean and the water evaporates into vapor. Up high, the vapor cools and condenses into clouds. When the clouds get heavy, it falls back down as rain or snow. Rivers and groundwater carry it back to the sea, and the cycle starts again.

So the water in your glass might be millions of years old.
scripts.roman:
They say all roads lead to Rome. On this map you can see why. From Rome, the Via Appia ran south all the way to Brindisi. Other roads crossed Gaul, Hispania and even Britain. Milestones marked every Roman mile along the trade routes.

That network held an empire together for centuries.
scripts.cpr: Someone collapses in front of you. What do you do? Follow this chart. First, check the scene is safe and call emergency services. Then put your hands in the center of the chest. Push hard and fast, about one hundred to one hundred twenty compressions a minute. Let the chest rise between compressions and keep going until help arrives.
scripts.unrelated: My grandmother made bread every Sunday. The kitchen smelled like yeast and butter. She never measured anything. She said the dough tells you when it is ready. I still think about her hands when I bake.
scripts.animation:
Ever wonder how a cartoon actually moves? It doesn't. Every second is twenty four still drawings.

An animator draws the key poses first: where the jump starts and where it lands. Then the frames in between fill the motion.

Your eyes hold each picture for a split second, so the drawings blur into movement. That's why a flip book works too.
